# Process capability and robustness {#sec-cap}

@tbl-cap gives the capability at commercial scale, from the integrated process model of the train (@sec-stats), of the drug substance attributes to which this step contributes.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(cap_tab, "Commercial-scale capability of the drug substance attributes to which the Protein A step contributes.", "tbl-cap",
        align=["P{3.9cm}", "c", "l", "r", "l", "c", "r"],
        notes=[("a)", "Not meaningful, because the simulated values lie below the LOQ and cannot be measured."),
               ("b)", "Below the limit of quantitation (LOQ) of the ELISA, " + g(lpa_loq) + " ppm (AMV-3016)."),
               ("", "Crit., criticality. Mean and range of the " + mc_n + " simulated batches. Limiting side, the limit of the "
                    "criterion nearer to the simulated batches.")]).show()
```

Host cell protein and fragments have Cpk values of `{python} f2(cpk['hcp'])` and `{python} f2(cpk['fragments_lmw'])`, above the target of `{python} f2(CPK_TARGET)` of PCMP-001 §7.9. Residual DNA has no intermediate acceptance criterion, and it reaches a Cpk of `{python} f2(cpk['residual_dna'])` in the drug substance. The integrated process model carries a nominal DNA reduction for each chromatography step, `{python} g(dna_lrv_cfg['protein_a'])` log10 at Protein A, `{python} g(dna_lrv_cfg['cex'])` at cation exchange and `{python} g(dna_lrv_cfg['aex'])` at anion exchange. The platform history gives no worst-case DNA clearance for these steps (@sec-prior), so the Cpk of residual DNA rests on these nominal values. At this step the reduction measured at the centre points, `{python} f1(dna_lrv_min)` to `{python} f1(dna_lrv_max)` log10, is at or below the nominal value.

No simulated batch of `{python} mc_n` fell outside the drug substance criterion for host cell protein, leached Protein A, fragments or residual DNA. With none of `{python} mc_n` outside, the probability of an out-of-specification batch in the simulation is below `{python} f2(oos_bound)` % at `{python} f"{100 * conf:.0f}"` % confidence. The bound does not include the uncertainty of the integrated process model itself.

The Cpk of leached Protein A is not meaningful. The simulated drug substance values average `{python} g(lpa_ds_mean)` ppm, below the limit of quantitation of the ELISA (`{python} g(lpa_loq)` ppm, AMV-3016). They cannot be measured, and their spread is that of the model, not of a result. Leached Protein A is judged instead against its criteria in the pool (@sec-par) and in the drug substance.

Acidic variants have the lowest Cpk of the drug substance, `{python} f2(cpk['acidic_variants'])`, set by the lower limit of `{python} g(acid_lim[0])` %. This is below the target of `{python} f2(CPK_TARGET)` and above the minimum of `{python} f2(CPK_MIN)` of PCMP-001 §7.9, which asks PCMR-001 to state the parameters that drive it. In the simulation `{python} acid_oos` batch of `{python} mc_n` fell outside the criterion, and the normal tail probability is `{python} f0(acid_ppm)` per million. The Protein A step does not separate charge variants. The hold of the eluate raises acidic variants slightly (@sec-hold), which is away from the lower limit that sets the Cpk.

# Parameter classification {#sec-class}

Parameters were classified under SOP-4001 by the decision logic of PCMP-001 §7.7. A parameter whose effect on a CQA is significant and practically relevant is critical. A critical parameter is a WC-CPP when it has a low risk of leaving its acceptable range in operation, and a CPP otherwise. A KPP affects only process performance, and a GPP has no relevant effect. The practical-relevance rule of PCP-005 §7 (criterion 8) states that an effect on an attribute is practically relevant when the NOR-propagated PAR of the parameter is narrower than its range studied. It also states that a significant effect whose PAR spans the whole range studied does not by itself make the parameter critical. The rule identifies the effect of elution buffer pH on pool host cell protein as practically relevant, because its NOR-propagated PAR, `{python} par_ph_hcp`, is narrower than its range studied (@sec-par). Every other NOR-propagated PAR spans its range studied, so the rule identifies no other parameter on its own. The class of each parameter therefore also rests on the size of its effects, on whether an effect takes an attribute beyond its criterion within the range studied, and on how readily the parameter is controlled. The classes and the reason for each are the following.

- Protein load was classified as a WC-CPP. It raises pool host cell protein by a factor of `{python} f2(fac_A)` across its range studied. Together with elution buffer pH it takes pool host cell protein above its criterion within the range studied, and `{python} n_hcp_over` results of the designs at the corner of high load and low pH exceeded the criterion (@sec-rsm-hcp). The load is set from the load volume and the titre of the clarified harvest by Protein A affinity HPLC (AMV-3021). It is readily controlled within its NOR of `{python} nor(P['load'])` g/L resin, inside a PAR that spans the range studied of `{python} rng(P['load'])` g/L resin. The NOR in force was narrowed in this revision from `{python} nor_load_c` g/L resin, the NOR as characterized, because over that NOR the scale-down model is not qualified for pool host cell protein (@sec-sdm).
- Elution buffer pH was classified as a WC-CPP. It has the largest effect on pool host cell protein, a factor of `{python} f2(fac_B)` across its range studied, which criterion 8 identifies as practically relevant, and fragments fall slightly as it rises. With protein load it bounds the design space. Buffer pH is controlled at preparation and verified at release. Its NOR-propagated PAR for pool host cell protein, `{python} par_ph_hcp`, is wide against its NOR of `{python} nor(P['elution_ph'])`, whose lower edge lies `{python} f2(par_ph_margin)` pH units inside the PAR. The deviation DEV-005-01 showed that a buffer below the NOR can pass release when the pH meter is incorrectly calibrated (@sec-dev01).
- Load flow rate was classified as a KPP. It lowers step yield at high load, because a faster load shortens the residence time and lowers the dynamic binding capacity. Its only effect on a CQA is the curvature of pool host cell protein, a rise of at most `{python} f"{flow_nor:.0f}"` % within its NOR and `{python} f"{max(flow_lo, flow_hi):.0f}"` % across its range studied. Within the NOR that does not move pool host cell protein appreciably against its criterion. Its NOR-propagated PAR spans the range studied for every output, so the practical-relevance rule does not make it critical. No effect of load flow rate on leached Protein A or fragments was detected within the range studied.
- End of pool collect was classified as a KPP. It has the largest effect on step yield. It also lowers pool host cell protein, by `{python} f"{fall_D:.0f}"` % across its range studied and `{python} f"{fall_D_nor:.0f}"` % across its NOR, and the sign of that effect differs between the designs (finding F11). The effect does not take pool host cell protein beyond its criterion with the other parameters within their NORs, and its PAR spans the range studied. The class would be revisited if a later study confirmed the screening sign.
- Operating temperature was classified as a GPP. No difference from the set-point runs was detected in pool host cell protein, step yield or leached Protein A at either end of its range. The intervals allow a rise in pool host cell protein of up to `{python} f0(uni_ub['temperature'])` ng/mg. Such a rise would still leave pool host cell protein within its criterion at manufacturing scale, and every individual result met its criterion (@sec-uni). The class rests on the attributes measured. Fragments were not measured in the univariate study, and a higher temperature could speed hinge hydrolysis during elution.
- Bed height was classified as a GPP. No difference from the set-point runs was detected in pool host cell protein, step yield or leached Protein A at either end of its range. The intervals allow a rise in pool host cell protein of up to `{python} f0(uni_ub['bed_height'])` ng/mg, and every individual result met its criterion (@sec-uni). Bed height is fixed by the packing specification of the commercial column and does not vary in operation. A short bed at the upper end of the load range was not characterized, and no claim is made for it. The class rests on the attributes measured. Fragments were not measured in the univariate study, and a shorter bed shortens the residence time, which could change the capture of fragments.

In summary the step has `{python} n_wc` WC-CPPs, `{python} n_kpp` KPPs and `{python} n_gpp` GPPs. `{python} "No parameter is in the class CPP" if n_cpp == 0 else f"{n_cpp} parameters are in the class CPP"`. The two WC-CPPs are critical parameters that are well controlled. The classes of protein load and elution buffer pH rest on the size of their effects on pool host cell protein, on criterion 8 for elution buffer pH, and on the corner where the two together take it above its criterion. Both effects agree in direction with the A-Mab case study. The KPP classes rest on the model for step yield, on the direction of the yield effects in both designs, and on the mechanism of breakthrough and of peak collection.

# Contribution to the control strategy {#sec-cs}

The Protein A step contributes to the control strategy in the following ways.

1. Process parameters. Protein load and elution buffer pH are controlled within their NORs as WC-CPPs, and load flow rate and end of pool collect within their NORs as KPPs. The NORs are those of PCP-005, except that of protein load, which this revision narrowed to `{python} nor(P['load'])` g/L resin (@sec-sdm). Movement outside the NOR and within the PARs of @sec-par is assessed under change control.
2. Material controls. Elution buffer is released against its pH specification, on a calibrated pH meter (DEV-005-01).
3. Resin and load. The protein load is set from the titre of the clarified harvest by Protein A affinity HPLC (AMV-3021). Leached Protein A is highest on new resin and is expected to rise with the protease activity of the load. Resin use, cleaning and sanitization are controlled by SOP-2008. The hold of the clarified harvest before capture, the expected cause of the offset of leached Protein A between the scales, is characterized in PCR-004.
4. Hold. An eluate made at set-point may be held at elution pH for up to `{python} h_days` days at `{python} t_cold` or `{python} t_warm` before viral inactivation. An eluate made at other settings within the NOR was not held (@sec-hold).
5. Downstream clearance. Host cell protein, leached Protein A and fragments are further cleared by cation exchange (PCR-007) and anion exchange (PCR-008). The criterion for pool host cell protein relies on cation exchange clearing host cell protein at least `{python} g(cex_req)`-fold, its platform worst case, and anion exchange at least `{python} T.num(aex_req)`-fold, its single-batch bound, while both run within their NORs (@sec-par). Host cell protein is tested at release of the drug substance. Viral clearance is claimed at low-pH viral inactivation (PCR-006), anion exchange and virus filtration (PCR-009), and not at this step.

The control strategy of the whole train is consolidated in PCMR-001.

# Discussion

The characterization confirms the main effects expected for this step. Elution buffer pH and protein load have the largest effects on pool host cell protein, and on the log scale their effects multiply. Whether a further interaction of the two exists the data do not decide (@sec-rsm-hcp). End of pool collect, protein load and load flow rate have the largest effects on step yield. Leached Protein A shows no dependence on the parameters within the range studied, and fragments depend only slightly on elution buffer pH. End of pool collect lowers pool host cell protein in the response-surface design but raised it, not significantly, in the screening design, for a reason that was not identified.

Model selection gave leached Protein A and fragments models that meet the adequacy criteria on lack of fit and predictive power, which their full quadratic models do not. The choice of model is a discrepancy from the plan, so its effect on the conclusions was examined. The conclusion over the NOR is the same with each of the `{python} n_near` models within 2 AICc units of the selected model of pool host cell protein, and with run `{python} dev_run` analysed in each of three ways.

The qualification of the scale-down model for pool host cell protein holds over the NOR in force and not over the protein load NOR as characterized. It rests on the widened criterion, on the `{python} n_sd_supp` set-point runs added after the planned runs had been analysed, and on the choice of the selected model (@sec-sdm). The offsets were estimated at set-point only. The report therefore assumes that the ratio for pool host cell protein and the difference for leached Protein A are the same across the ranges studied, and this assumption is not tested. Fragments have no measured offset. Their conclusions assume no difference between the scales, on the mechanism of capture and on the bound from the hold study of the clarified harvest (@sec-sdm).

The criterion for pool host cell protein links this step to the two later steps. It credits cation exchange with its platform worst case of `{python} g(cex_req)`-fold, above the single-batch bound of `{python} T.num(cex_bound)`-fold of its A-Mab model, and anion exchange with its single-batch bound of `{python} T.num(aex_req)`-fold. The control of this step therefore depends on the control of those steps (PCR-007, PCR-008), and an excursion would be detected at release of the drug substance (@sec-par).

No selected model meets criterion 5, and the conclusions rest on the influence analysis and on the size of the two residual trends (PD-005-02). The re-assay of run `{python} dev_005_02_run` decides whether leached Protein A depends on end of pool collect, but not its judgement against the criterion (@sec-dev02). Each design used one feed, so the effect of feed quality was not estimated. The univariate study cannot detect interactions, has `{python} uni_reps` runs at each end, takes its reference from the qualification study and did not measure fragments. The hold study held one eluate, made at set-point.

# Conclusions

1. The step was characterized under PCP-005 in a screening design, a response-surface design, a univariate study and a hold study.
2. The scale-down model is qualified by its offset for leached Protein A and, over the NOR in force, for pool host cell protein. Over the protein load NOR as characterized, `{python} nor_load_c` g/L resin, it is not qualified for pool host cell protein, and the NOR of protein load in force was narrowed to `{python} nor(P['load'])` g/L resin. The qualification for pool host cell protein also rests on the widened criterion, on all `{python} n_sd_all` set-point runs and on the selected model. Fragments carry no offset, and their conclusions assume no difference between the scales.
3. Each output of the response-surface design was analysed by model selection. Each selected model meets the adequacy criteria on lack of fit and predictive power, and each model with a term is significant. No model meets criterion 5, and the conclusions rest on the analyses of PD-005-02.
4. Elution buffer pH and protein load have the largest effects on pool host cell protein, and their main effects multiply. End of pool collect, protein load and load flow rate have the largest effects on step yield. Leached Protein A shows no dependence on the parameters within the range studied, on the re-assay of run `{python} dev_005_02_run`, and fragments fall slightly as elution buffer pH rises.
5. The criterion for pool host cell protein, ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg, is widened by the single-batch bound of anion exchange. The widening is the producer's risk, and an excursion would be detected at release of the drug substance.
6. Each output with a criterion met it across the NOR in force. Every NOR-propagated PAR spans the range studied of its parameter, except that of elution buffer pH for pool host cell protein, `{python} par_ph_hcp`. On its median predictions pool host cell protein exceeds its criterion only at high protein load combined with low elution buffer pH, never with both inside their NORs.
7. Protein load and elution buffer pH are WC-CPPs, load flow rate and end of pool collect are KPPs, and operating temperature and bed height are GPPs. No parameter is in the class CPP.
8. For operating temperature and bed height, no difference from the set-point runs was detected in pool host cell protein, step yield or leached Protein A, and their ranges studied are supported for these attributes with the other parameters at their set-points.
9. An eluate made at set-point may be held at elution pH for `{python} h_days` days at `{python} t_cold` or `{python} t_warm`, and the hold meets criterion 7 for every attribute it changes.
10. At commercial scale the Cpk of host cell protein and of fragments exceeds the target of `{python} f2(CPK_TARGET)`. Leached Protein A is judged on the pool and in the drug substance against its criteria.
11. The `{python} n_dev` deviations were investigated and their runs retained, and the `{python} n_pd` discrepancies from the plan are recorded in @sec-dev. The results roll up into PCMR-001.

# Deviations and discrepancies from the plan {#sec-dev}

A deviation is a departure from an approved procedure or a GMP requirement, or an unplanned event during execution. A discrepancy from the plan is work that the approved plan did not foresee and that was done under approved procedures, such as further runs or a further analysis. The deviation register lists `{python} n_dev` deviations for the studies of the step (@tbl-dev). Both were investigated, and their runs were retained.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(md_rows(dev_register(DOC)), "Deviations recorded for the studies of the Protein A step.", "tbl-dev",
        align=["l", "P{4.4cm}", "P{5.6cm}", "l"], size="footnotesize").show()
```

## DEV-005-01. Elution buffer pH below target on a response-surface run {#sec-dev01}

The elution buffer of lot `{python} dev_lot` was used on run `{python} dev_run` of the response-surface design, whose design setting for elution buffer pH was `{python} g(dev_ph_design)`. During preparation the titration of the buffer overshot its end point, and the buffer was at pH `{python} g(dev_005_01_ph_measured)`, `{python} f2(dev_ph_gap)` pH units below its target. It passed release because the pH meter used for release was incorrectly calibrated and read it within its specification. The recorded pH is below the NOR of `{python} nor(P['elution_ph'])` and inside the range studied of `{python} rng(P['elution_ph'])`.

Run `{python} dev_run` is analysed at its recorded pH, the setting at which it was made. PCP-005 planned every run at its design setting, so this is the discrepancy from the plan PD-005-03 (@sec-pd-analysis). The run gave a pool host cell protein of `{python} f0(dev_obs_m)` ng/mg at manufacturing scale, below the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg. On the selected model its residual is `{python} mn(f2(dev_res))` on the natural log scale. The result is therefore `{python} f"{dev_res_pct:.0f}"` % below the median predicted at pH `{python} g(dev_ph_rec)`, `{python} f0(dev_pred_rec)` ng/mg, which is `{python} f1(dev_res_sd)` residual standard deviations. Its Cook's distance, `{python} f2(dev_cook)`, is above the limit of 4/n. At the design pH of `{python} g(dev_ph_design)` the same model predicts `{python} f0(dev_pred_des)` ng/mg, closer to the result. The result does not show the full rise in pool host cell protein that a buffer at the recorded pH would be expected to cause. The data do not establish why.

@tbl-dev01 gives the conclusion for pool host cell protein with run `{python} dev_run` analysed in three ways, each with the model selection repeated.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(sens_df, "Selected model of pool HCP and its upper prediction limit over the NOR (ng/mg, manufacturing scale) with run " + str(dev_run) + " analysed in three ways.", "tbl-dev01",
        align=["P{4.4cm}", "c", "P{3.9cm}", "r", "r", "c"],
        notes=[("", "Terms of the selected model besides the intercept, coded as in the factor legend. AB, the interaction of A with B. "
                    "A², C², the squares of A and C. At the estimate and at the low end, the upper prediction limit with the offset "
                    "ratio at its estimate and at the low end of its interval. Met, both limits within the criterion of ≤ "
                    + crit_hcp + " ng/mg.")]).show()
```

With run `{python} dev_run` at its design pH, or excluded, the log scale is chosen again, and the selection adds the interaction of protein load with elution buffer pH and the square of protein load. The interaction is not significant in the full quadratic model on the log scale in any of the three analyses (`{python} pf(SENS['recorded']['p_ab'])`, `{python} f3(SENS['design']['p_ab'])` and `{python} f3(SENS['excluded']['p_ab'])`). Nor is it significant in the two selected models that contain it (`{python} pf(SSEL['design']['p_ab'])` and `{python} f3(SSEL['excluded']['p_ab'])`). In the selected model with the run at its design pH the square of protein load is negative (`{python} pf(sens_a2['p_a2'])`), so in that analysis the rise of pool host cell protein with load levels off at high load. In all three analyses pool host cell protein meets its criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg at every combination of the NOR, with the offset ratio at its estimate and at the unfavourable end of its interval. The qualification of the scale-down model is therefore the same however run `{python} dev_run` is analysed. The analysis at the recorded pH gives the highest upper prediction limit of the three. The run was retained, and it carries a footnote in Appendix B.

## DEV-005-02. Leached Protein A result of run `{python} dev_005_02_run` initially out of trend {#sec-dev02}

The leached Protein A result of run `{python} dev_005_02_run` of the response-surface design was out of trend at analytical review. The first result was `{python} f2(dev02_first)` ppm in the scale-down model, `{python} f2(dev02_first_m)` ppm at manufacturing scale. The sample was re-assayed under AMV-3016, and the re-assay gave `{python} f2(dev02_val)` ppm, `{python} f2(dev02_m)` ppm at manufacturing scale. The first result was `{python} g(first_ratio)` times the re-assay. The investigation suspected carryover in the ELISA, which would add analyte from a preceding sample, and did not confirm it. The re-assay result is the one reported in Appendix B and used in the analysis, because the investigation attributed the first result to that suspected cause. The first result was kept in the record with its status marked. Both results lie inside the range of the other runs of the design, and both are far below the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_lpa` ppm.

With the first result in place of the re-assay, the analysis changes. The model selection then keeps end of pool collect, and that model is not significant (`{python} pf(s02_p)`). It fails criterion 2, so leached Protein A would be judged on its measured results. Every result of both designs then meets the criterion, the highest at `{python} f2(lpa_first_max_m)` ppm at manufacturing scale. The trend of the residuals on run order is then not significant (`{python} pf(order_p_first)`). The judgement of leached Protein A against its criterion is therefore the same with either result. Whether leached Protein A depends on end of pool collect, and whether its residuals drift with run order, depends on which result is used.

## Discrepancies from the plan

The report records `{python} n_pd` discrepancies from the plan (@tbl-pd). They are judged against PCP-005 Version 2.0, the plan this report is written against. That version includes the retest of retained samples, S-PA-RET, made under the method decision AMD-001, so S-PA-RET is not a discrepancy.

### PD-005-01. Supplementary set-point runs in the scale-down model qualification {#sec-pd01}

PCP-005 planned `{python} n_sd_plan` set-point runs of the scale-down model in the qualification study S-PA-SDM, compared with `{python} n_m` manufacturing-scale batches. During the Version 2.0 re-analysis, while INV-001 was open, a further `{python} n_sd_supp` set-point runs were made in study S-PA-SDM2 (`{python} win('S-PA-SDM2')`), under the same procedures as the planned runs. @tbl-sdm-offsets-planned gives the qualification on the `{python} n_sd_plan` planned runs alone.

On the planned runs alone the scale-down model is not qualified for pool host cell protein, even over the NOR in force. The ratio is `{python} rt0_hcp` (`{python} rt0_hcp_lo` to `{python} rt0_hcp_hi`) on the planned runs and `{python} rt_hcp` (`{python} rt_hcp_lo` to `{python} rt_hcp_hi`) on all runs. With the ratio at the low end of the wider interval, the upper prediction limit over the NOR is `{python} f0(pl_lo0)` ng/mg, above the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg, while at the estimate of the ratio the criterion is met. The further runs narrowed the half-width of the interval on the log scale by `{python} f"{narrow_pct:.0f}"` %, and this made the qualification possible. For leached Protein A the model is qualified on the planned runs as well, with the scale-down model `{python} lpa0_off` ppm lower (`{python} lpa0_off_a` to `{python} lpa0_off_b` ppm lower).

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.sdm_offsets(["protein_a"], studies=["S-PA-SDM"], label="tbl-sdm-offsets-planned").show()
```

The decision to make the runs was taken during the re-analysis, after the result on the planned runs was known. The qualification for pool host cell protein therefore rests on runs added after a result was seen. Runs added until a test passes raise the chance that it passes, and this is a limitation of that qualification. The rule of qualification and the criterion were not changed because of the further runs. Only the number of runs grew. The centre points of the designs are also set-point runs of the scale-down model. They were not added to the offset, because PCP-005 §5.1 defines the qualification on the runs of the qualification study.

### PD-005-02 to PD-005-04. Changes to the analysis {#sec-pd-analysis}

The other three discrepancies change how the runs are analysed, and each is described where its result is reported.

- PD-005-02. PCP-005 planned to set the ranges and the design space from models that meet every model adequacy criterion of PCP-005 §7. No selected model meets criterion 5, and the conclusions rest instead on an influence analysis and on the size of each residual trend against the criterion of its output (@sec-resid).
- PD-005-03. Run `{python} dev_run` is analysed at the elution buffer pH recorded under DEV-005-01, the setting at which it was made, and not at its design setting (@sec-dev01).
- PD-005-04. Each output was analysed by model selection (@sec-stats) in place of the full quadratic model of PCP-005 §5.5, as `{python} INV2['id']` corrective action CA3 requires of every report. PCMP-001 Version 2.0 still names the full quadratic model, so the selection is a discrepancy from the plan. The selected models are in @tbl-adequacy.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(md_rows(discrepancy_register(DOC)), "Discrepancies of this report from its plan PCP-005.", "tbl-pd",
        align=["l", "P{2.2cm}", "P{3.0cm}", "P{4.6cm}", "P{3.3cm}"], size="footnotesize").show()
```
